problem.problem:
Bob is green. Bob is kind. Charlie is green. Charlie is not smart. Erin is not young. Fiona is nice. Fiona is young. Green, smart things are quiet. If something is kind then it is green. Smart things are young. Young things are kind. Quiet things are furry. All quiet, nice things are furry. Nice, green things are smart. If Bob is kind and Bob is not green then Bob is furry.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Bob is furry.

Predicates:
Green($x, bool) ::: Is x green?
Kind($x, bool) ::: Is x kind?
Smart($x, bool) ::: Is x smart?
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?
Quiet($x, bool) ::: Is x quiet?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?
Nice($x, bool) ::: Is x nice?

Facts:
Green(Bob, True) ::: Bob is green.
Kind(Bob, True) ::: Bob is kind.
Green(Charlie, True) ::: Charlie is green.
Smart(Charlie, False) ::: Charlie is not smart.
Young(Erin, False) ::: Erin is not young.
Nice(Fiona, True) ::: Fiona is nice.
Young(Fiona, True) ::: Fiona is young.

Rules:
Green($x, True) && Smart($x, True) >>> Quiet($x, True) ::: Green, smart things are quiet.
Kind($x, True) >>> Green($x, True) ::: If something is kind then it is green.
Smart($x, True) >>> Young($x, True) ::: Smart things are young.
Young($x, True) >>> Kind($x, True) ::: Young things are kind.
Quiet($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: Quiet things are furry.
Quiet($x, True) && Nice($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: All quiet, nice things are furry.
Nice($x, True) && Green($x, True) >>> Smart($x, True) ::: Nice, green things are smart.
Kind(Bob, True) && Green(Bob, False) >>> Furry(Bob, True) ::: If Bob is kind and Bob is not green then Bob is furry.

Query:
Furry(Bob, True) ::: Bob is furry.
